title: How National Highways is using #knowledgegraphs to achieve shared meaning #visualstorytelling
description:
National Highways is a major infrastructure company that builds, manages and operates the strategic road network across England. It has taken a long-term approach to building a digital twin of the organisation, by paying attention not just to the need for semantic interoperability between datasets, but to the need for corresponding shared meaning between the people who own and work with those datasets.

This talk walks through the approach taken in its shared meaning programme and demonstrate Compass, a platform that makes the underlying RDF knowledge graph intuitive and accessible to members of staff and suppliers alike.

It also demonstrates some of the lessons learned about how to gain organisational traction and demonstrate ROI, and share some conceptual principles that will have relevance for anyone trying to bridge silos in large, complex organisations.

Link to talk: https://2025.connected-data.london/talks/compass-how-national-highways-is-using-knowledge-graphs-to-achieve-shared-meaning/

--

Gergely Raccuja. Principal Product Owner, Highways England

Co-leader of the data science team at National Highways and data product owner of Compass.

Steve Whitla. Founder, Visual Meaning

Steve Whitla is the founder and director of Visual Meaning, a company that combines systems thinking, visual thinking and semantic modelling to help large organisations make sense of complexity.
